assumptions: When explicitly configured by allow_none_return, a statically known None return is an unprotected absence marker; effect obligations are still checked. No other value is exempted.
Explicit refusing-authorizer primitives return only after enforcing authorization; every denial raises. This is a trusted primitive contract, never inferred from a helper's name.

ReadSource primitives return fresh inert data without granting authority; acquisition-side permissions require separate Operation contracts. For publication proofs, trusted primitive failures carry no protected payload. Return obligations apply to every discovered entry and bind the exact result; literal refusals contain no protected payload.
Authorizer primitives authenticate inputs and return the declared Decision for exactly their bound arguments.
Operation primitives are the complete terminal effect boundary in the supplied source universe.

Imports, builtin data operations, standard dataclass construction, native method binding, override metadata, builtin exceptions and Verdict identity have their declared meanings; custom descriptors and monkeypatching are outside the model.

Field-only typing/typing_extensions NamedTuple classes with postponed annotations and immutable literal defaults use native constructors, tuple projections, _replace and _asdict. Nested mutable fields retain alias dependencies. Custom record methods, subclasses, unmodeled generated members and generated API surfaces require additional models; annotations do not establish input shapes.

Standard typing and typing_extensions TYPE_CHECKING is False at runtime; cast returns its val argument unchanged after evaluating and binding all arguments. A cast establishes no runtime type or authorization.

Supported inert TypedDict declarations use the native typing/typing_extensions metaclass: construction produces an ordinary dict without schema validation and isinstance against the declaration raises TypeError. Annotations grant no runtime types or authority.

Native ContextVar get/set/reset operates in one current execution context across direct source calls and awaits. Module variables may contain inherited values; local variables start unset. Task creation, context copying/switching, external context mutation, token context managers and arbitrary context introspection require separate models.

Statically named ordinary source bases follow native C3 method resolution. Bound super proxies use the lexical starting class and the actual receiver's method order; custom metaclasses, dynamic bases, unbound super descriptors and generated dataclass class cells require additional models.

Lazy export resolution uses ordinary source-module imports with native importlib semantics and inert native import-error diagnostics; custom import hooks and external mutation of module bindings/export tables are outside the model. Every source initializer is still checked.
Standard reentrant locks use the native _thread.RLock context protocol: enter returns True and exit does not suppress exceptions or invoke user callbacks. This is not a concurrency proof.
Security inputs change only through modeled writes; external concurrent mutation, including across awaits, is outside the model.
Terminal return values and exception payloads contain inert data, never executable or receiver capabilities.

Input truth tests and keyword-key hashing/equality are stable and inert; custom input protocols and concurrent mutation require another model. Python keyword packing alone does not establish inert key protocols.
Ordinary helper bodies are analyzed, never accepted through opaque reviewed-call exemptions.

proof.property: Every reachable terminal dispatch and every declared API-return obligation on every modelled path consumes a fresh ALLOW decision for identical bindings.
proof.scope: Closed-world supported Python subset under explicit terminal and object-model contracts; not arbitrary Python or policy semantics.

publications.scope: Effective-return obligations, not adapter or system completeness. Backing acquisition is opaque for this property only. Unmodeled router receivers/results remain unresolved, including escalation; no routed-value grant is assumed.

remaining_proof_obligations: Every protected effect reaches a refusing route, including inherited APIs, every supported input shape, callbacks, exceptional paths, and publication channels.
Object policy and effects preserve authoritative identity, labels, transformations, approval bindings, and atomicity across each adapter.
Untrusted workers have no coordinator capabilities and use authenticated object channels; node-host protocol conformance alone does not prove process isolation.
Host adapters install exactly or tighter grants before execution and preserve confinement through cancellation and descendant lifetime. MAC/LSM correctness is assumed.

router.claim: Every admitted HostRouter entry authorizes the identical effective request before atomic dispatch; tool calls preserve constraints, and cross-tool entries additionally require fresh authenticated-origin, delegation and tool-transition decisions.
router.scope: HostRouter's entire discovered method surface, including the generic framework-object route. Host-confined ToolNode and guarded_tool calls enter the tool-call surface through a separately tested exact-decision bridge.

assumptions: When explicitly configured by allow_none_return, a statically known None return is an unprotected absence marker; effect obligations are still checked. No other value is exempted.
Explicit refusing-authorizer primitives return only after enforcing authorization; every denial raises. This is a trusted primitive contract, never inferred from a helper's name.

ReadSource primitives return fresh inert data without granting authority; acquisition-side permissions require separate Operation contracts. For publication proofs, trusted primitive failures carry no protected payload. Return obligations apply to every discovered entry and bind the exact result; literal refusals contain no protected payload.
Authorizer primitives authenticate inputs and return the declared Decision for exactly their bound arguments.
Operation primitives are the complete terminal effect boundary in the supplied source universe.

Imports, builtin data operations, standard dataclass construction, native method binding, override metadata, builtin exceptions and Verdict identity have their declared meanings; custom descriptors and monkeypatching are outside the model.

Field-only typing/typing_extensions NamedTuple classes with postponed annotations and immutable literal defaults use native constructors, tuple projections, _replace and _asdict. Nested mutable fields retain alias dependencies. Custom record methods, subclasses, unmodeled generated members and generated API surfaces require additional models; annotations do not establish input shapes.

Standard typing and typing_extensions TYPE_CHECKING is False at runtime; cast returns its val argument unchanged after evaluating and binding all arguments. A cast establishes no runtime type or authorization.

Supported inert TypedDict declarations use the native typing/typing_extensions metaclass: construction produces an ordinary dict without schema validation and isinstance against the declaration raises TypeError. Annotations grant no runtime types or authority.

Native ContextVar get/set/reset operates in one current execution context across direct source calls and awaits. Module variables may contain inherited values; local variables start unset. Task creation, context copying/switching, external context mutation, token context managers and arbitrary context introspection require separate models.

Statically named ordinary source bases follow native C3 method resolution. Bound super proxies use the lexical starting class and the actual receiver's method order; custom metaclasses, dynamic bases, unbound super descriptors and generated dataclass class cells require additional models.

Lazy export resolution uses ordinary source-module imports with native importlib semantics and inert native import-error diagnostics; custom import hooks and external mutation of module bindings/export tables are outside the model. Every source initializer is still checked.
Standard reentrant locks use the native _thread.RLock context protocol: enter returns True and exit does not suppress exceptions or invoke user callbacks. This is not a concurrency proof.
Security inputs change only through modeled writes; external concurrent mutation, including across awaits, is outside the model.
Terminal return values and exception payloads contain inert data, never executable or receiver capabilities.

Input truth tests and keyword-key hashing/equality are stable and inert; custom input protocols and concurrent mutation require another model. Python keyword packing alone does not establish inert key protocols.
Ordinary helper bodies are analyzed, never accepted through opaque reviewed-call exemptions.

trusted_boundary: Host MAC/LSM correctly enforces installed policy for every resource access.
The host adapter binds principal, request, tool and all constraints, activates confinement before tool imports/initialization/execution, and never falls back to control-process execution.
The host authenticates origin against a live worker channel and binds it again at nested dispatch; caller-supplied origin strings are not credentials.
Workers cannot use root admission or acquire another registered tool's authority through a raw callable, direct service channel, or unmediated host API.
Policy decisions implement the intended policy; inputs and service bindings are immutable throughout a call; the Python control plane and construction are trusted.
